prior_findings.N1: RESOLVED. Contract line 13 now makes the tenancy interceptor keep the exact actor it passes to hasActiveMembership. It writes mode:'protected' only when that actor equals the patched RequestContext.actorId and request.principal.id, and the checked tenant equals the patched RequestContext.tenantId and STYNX_VERIFIED_TENANT_ID. On mismatch nothing is written, so the command fails before SQL or handler. This matches the source. resolveActorId (tenant-context.interceptor.ts:176-180) is stynxClaims.sub ?? unverified bearer sub ?? principal.id. Once AuthContextGuard clears stynxClaims, a mapper can set principal.id (auth-context.guard.ts:82-86,114-115) to something other than the bearer sub. Tenancy then checks the bearer sub, the comparison fails and no port entry is written. The contract states that the membership lookup and non-command behavior are unchanged; writing to the port is additive. Prompt 61 has the matching sensor (mapper principal.id ≠ bearer sub → no result, reject before command SQL or handler). Prompt 62 specifies the same rule, including tenant equality.
prior_findings.N2: RESOLVED. Line 15 states that imperative app.useGlobalGuards is unsupported command provenance, including before app.init(), and gives the reason: Nest 11 has no public DI registry for ApplicationConfig.globalGuards. A command whose only guard is registered that way fails the boot check. Discovery is limited to route/class @UseGuards metadata and APP_GUARD providers, both reachable through Reflector/ModulesContainer. Prompt 61 tests route/class and APP_GUARD registrations and rejects useGlobalGuards even before init. Prompt 62 excludes it. The plan checkpoint says the same.
prior_findings.N3: RESOLVED. Line 13 requires that mode:'verified' has actorId === request.principal.id, and that any stynxClaims.sub and .tenantId equal that principal and the Host-selected tenant; otherwise no entry and rejection before SQL. The source agrees: verifiedActor is stynxClaims.sub ?? principal.id (line 97), and both guards set principal.id to the verified subject or clear claims on public entry. Prompts 61 and 62 match.
prior_findings.N4: RESOLVED. Line 15 requires the brand as an own property, checked with Object.hasOwn and === true on the concrete metatype or instance constructor. A same-name look-alike and a subclass that only inherits the brand both fail. Deliberate self-branding is stated to fall inside the in-process trusted-code boundary. Prompt 61 tests look-alike and subclass rejection. Prompt 62 requires an own brand on the concrete constructor and never a class name or inherited brand.

findings.title: Residual 'as a global guard' wording is ambiguous after useGlobalGuards was excluded
findings.evidence: The same paragraph declares imperative app.useGlobalGuards unsupported. It then says a protected or optional-auth command requires a built-in guard 'on their route/class or as a global guard'. A reader could take 'global guard' to include app.useGlobalGuards, which contradicts the preceding sentence.
findings.required_change: Replace 'or as a global guard' with 'or as an `APP_GUARD` provider'. This is wording only and does not block.

findings.title: Engineer prompt says 'route/class/global guard metatypes' before the exclusion
findings.evidence: The prompt says 'inspect actual route/class/global guard metatypes or instances, excluding imperative app.useGlobalGuards'. The intent is clear, but naming APP_GUARD would match the contract and prompt 61 exactly. It would also point the Engineer at ModulesContainer provider discovery, where APP_GUARD tokens carry a generated suffix and request-scoped or useFactory providers need a metatype or instance constructor check, and away from ApplicationConfig internals.
findings.required_change: Say 'route/class @UseGuards metadata and APP_GUARD providers'. Optionally note that APP_GUARD provider tokens are discovered by prefix through ModulesContainer, without private Nest internals. This is wording only and does not block.

summary: The ae27eb5f revision resolves all four review-2 findings, and the source agrees. N1: tenancy attests the actor it actually checked for membership only when that actor equals principal.id, the patched context actor and the verified tenant, so a mapper-derived principal.id that differs from the bearer sub fails before command SQL. N2: imperative useGlobalGuards is explicitly unsupported; route/class and APP_GUARD are the supported and tested paths. N3: the verified public actor is bound to principal.id, with claims tied to that principal and the Host tenant. N4: only an own brand on the concrete constructor passes, and self-branding sits inside the trusted-code boundary. The prompts use matching sensors and paths. The plan records 42c069b9 as REVIEW and leaves the next SHA/PASS slot pending. Two LOW wording cleanups (both saying 'global guard' where APP_GUARD is meant) are advisory. This PASS does not dispatch the Inspector: the maestro must first record this revision's exact SHA and this PASS receipt in ctg-0005-plan.md.
